thread:
Erin (PM): posted a PRD draft for embedding dimension migrations + reranking edge-cases. main ask: support customer migrations (e.g. 384 -> 512) with minimal downtime and clear acceptance criteria. https://redwood.internal/prd/embed-migration :eyes:
Alice (EM): skimmed. can we clarify allowed strategies? reindex only, on-the-fly projection, or dual-index fallback? those have very different infra costs.
Ben (ML Eng): technically: rerank requires same-dim vectors for dot/cosine. options:
- reindex (preferred for correctness)
- online projection (learn small projection matrix) -> faster but may change ranking distribution
- pad with zeros (bad)
Carla (ML Research): padding kills cosine-based comparisons. projection needs evaluation: train mapping on representative dataset, measure MRR/ndcg. propose acceptance thresholds: MRR drop <1%, recall@10 drop <2%.
Dan (SRE): rollout notes: reindexing at scale needs throttled backfill, canary index swap, and rollback path. we should budget IO and GPU time. estimate for a 1B doc index -> ~48h on current infra unless we add burst capacity.
Jules (Sales): Acme quoted tight timeline: wants migration before end of quarter. they'll pay for dedicated backfill if ETA is clear. raising priority on commercial side.
Erin (PM): proposed MVP scope (to negotiate):
- Acceptance criteria:
  1) No downtime for query API (reads served from old index until swap).
  2) Reindex completes and canary swap validated with acceptance evals (Carla's metrics).
  3) Rollback possible within 1 hour via index pointer revert.
  4) Migration tooling documented + CLI for customers with dedicated capacity.
- Out of scope for MVP: auto-projection service, continuous on-the-fly conversions, cross-dim live merging.
Ben (ML Eng): implementation sketch:
- add backfill worker with batch semantics (idempotent, rate-limit).
- index format embeds dim metadata and version.
- add index-swap API: ``POST /v1/indexes/{id}/swap?from=canary``
- add metrics: backfill progress, per-batch latency, failed items.
Carla (ML Research): tests to run pre/post swap:
- A/B rerank test with held-out prompts.
- Evaluate embedding space drift: mean cosine shift, fraction of pairs that change sign.
- Edge cases: empty vectors, NaNs after quantization, mixed L2/L1 norms.
Dan (SRE): infra checklist:
- canary cluster with same qps profile
- throttled queue and auto-pause on error spikes
- alert: backfill-error-rate > 0.5% or index-swap delay > 2h
Ben (ML Eng): small helpful snippet for backfill CLI:
```
# example
redwood backfill-index --index docs-emb --from-dim 384 --to-dim 512 --batch-size 2048 --rate-limit 2000
```
Alice (EM): scope negotiation: given Acme timeline, we can try a small-pool pilot (1-2 customers) as MVP. full 1B reindex remains contingent on budget approval.
Jules (Sales): will confirm with Acme if pilot acceptable and if they want to pay for burst GPUs.
Erin (PM): owners and next steps:
- Ben -> infra + backfill worker (owner)
- Carla -> evaluation harness + acceptance tests (owner)
- Dan -> rollout runbook + alerts (owner)
- Alice -> coordinate customer pilot (owner)
- Jules -> commercial scoping with Acme
I'll update PRD to reflect MVP acceptance criteria and out-of-scope items, then ping infra/product boards. :thumbsup:
Ben (ML Eng): one more edge-case: embeddings created with different normalization pipelines (L2-normalized vs raw). decide canonical storage: store both raw and normalized? storing both doubles storage. prefer storing raw + normalization metadata so we can reproduce.
Carla (ML Research): agreed. add unit test: if metadata mismatch, backfill must either re-run normalization or fail with clear error.
Dan (SRE): create infra ticket for canary resources and estimated cost. I'll link it in the PRD.
Erin (PM): great thread — will push updated PRD by EOD and request a 30-min sync tomorrow to finalize acceptance criteria and sign-offs.
Jules (Sales): I'll loop in Acme and confirm pilot acceptance window.
Alice (EM): marking this thread as actionable. thanks everyone.
